The glass bottle had washed up on the rocks below, catching the last light of dusk like a trapped firefly. Maren pulled it from the tide pool, her fingers numb with cold.

Inside, a slip of paper, yellowed and soft as skin.

She unfolded it. Recognized her own handwriting—that peculiar backward tilt of the 'n', the way she crossed her t's like little swords.

*Maren—*

*Don't leave the light on past the third bell. When the storm comes, don't—*

The words stopped there. Torn. Or perhaps she'd only had time to write so much.

She read it again. A chill climbed her spine that had nothing to do with the wind.

She'd written this. She was certain. But she'd never written it. Never found such a bottle. Never stood on these rocks with salt on her lips and a strange, sweet grief tightening her chest.

The lighthouse beam swept across the water behind her. Once. Twice.

Somewhere below, the tide whispered secrets she almost remembered.
